remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review package provenance and install only the official @azure packages from trusted registries.

content.value_statement: Real-time voice apps need reliable streaming, events, and authentication. This skill guides Azure Voice Live setup, session configuration, and TypeScript integration.
actual_capabilities: Shows Microsoft Entra ID and optional API key authentication patterns.
Documents session setup for text, audio, voice, VAD, and audio formats.
Shows event handlers for audio, text, transcription, errors, and function calls.
Lists supported voice types, real-time models, and key SDK types.
limitations: Does not provide a complete microphone capture or playback implementation.
Requires an Azure AI resource and compatible model deployment.
Examples need local testing for browser permissions, codecs, and latency.
API key use should follow the user security policy.

use_cases.title: Voice Assistant Prototype
use_cases.description: Create a TypeScript starter plan for an Azure voice assistant with streaming audio and text responses.

use_cases.title: Customer Support Voice Bot
use_cases.description: Map session options, turn detection, voices, and function calling for a support workflow.

use_cases.title: Realtime Audio SDK Review
use_cases.description: Compare authentication, models, audio formats, and event handlers before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Voice Live Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start a TypeScript project that uses Azure AI Voice Live with Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Voice Live session for a voice assistant that supports text, audio, Azure Standard voice, and server VAD.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Streaming Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the event handling plan for connection, transcription, response text, response audio, errors, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Design Function Calling
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe function calling flow for Azure AI Voice Live that validates arguments and returns tool results.

output_examples.input: Create a quick start plan for an Azure Voice Live assistant.
output: Install the Azure Voice Live and identity packages.
Configure the Azure endpoint and credential source.
Start a session with a real-time model.
Subscribe to audio, text, transcription, and error events.
Close subscriptions when the session ends.

output_examples.input: Explain which session options matter for a browser voice app.
output_examples.output: The response names modalities, voice choice, turn detection, input and output audio format, microphone permission, and cleanup behavior.

output_examples.input: Plan a function calling workflow for weather support.
output_examples.output: The response describes tool schema design, argument validation, weather lookup, tool result delivery, and response continuation.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential before considering API key authentication.
Validate audio format, sample rate, and browser microphone permissions early.
Close subscriptions and handle connection, authentication, and protocol errors.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding API keys in examples, logs, or committed files.
Starting browser audio work without testing permission and codec behavior.
Ignoring cleanup for long-running WebSocket sessions.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build TypeScript voice AI apps with Azure AI Voice Live and streaming events.

faq.question: Does it support browser projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes browser guidance, but users must test permissions and bundler behavior.

faq.question: Which authentication method is preferred?
faq.answer: Microsoft Entra ID with DefaultAzureCredential is preferred over API key authentication.

faq.question: Does it include full audio capture code?
faq.answer: No. It references microphone access and audio processing but does not provide a complete player.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I validate before production use?
faq.answer: Validate authentication, model access, audio format, latency, error handling, and data retention requirements.
